title: Quotient module pullbacks respect normalized ordinary and derived composition
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with each $P_n=A/I^n$ finite, and put $R_T=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(P_m)_T$ and $Q_{T,n}=(P_n)_T$ as an $R_T$-module via its quotient projection. Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be composable scheme morphisms. Give their small pro-etale topoi the canonical coefficient identifications $c_u:u^{-1}R_{\mathrm{target}(u)}\cong R_{\mathrm{source}(u)}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], with the composite identification for $kh=k\circ h$. Use the actual module adjunctions and their exact derived pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For $u=h,k,kh$, let $a_{u,n}:u^*Q_{\mathrm{target}(u),n}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathrm{source}(u),n}$ be the coefficient-linear module comparison induced by $c_{u,n}$. Normalize its adjunct to send each constant section $p$ to the same constant section on the base-changed object. Let $D_{h,k}:k_*\circ h_*\cong(kh)_*$ denote the ordinary direct-image compositor; for every pro-etale object $U\to V$, its section map is restriction along $(Z\times_W(W\times_VU))\cong Z\times_VU$. Let $b_{h,k}:(kh)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*k^*$ be its inverse left-adjoint conjugate.

For every $n\geq1$, the ordinary module comparisons satisfy
$$a_{kh,n}=a_{h,n}\circ h^*a_{k,n}\circ b_{h,k,Q_{V,n}}.$$
Let $q_{u,n}:Lu^*Q_{\mathrm{target}(u),n}[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathrm{source}(u),n}[0]$ be the localization of $a_{u,n}$ with the canonical exact-pullback/single-complex comparisons. For the canonical derived compositor $c_{h,k}:L(kh)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lk^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], including transport along the completed coefficient identification, one has the equality in $D(R_Z)$
$$q_{kh,n}=q_{h,n}\circ Lh^*(q_{k,n})\circ c_{h,k,Q_{V,n}[0]}.$$
The ordinary and derived comparisons are natural in quotient transition maps and morphisms of the finite coefficient systems.

For $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to Y'$ forming a chosen Cartesian square $fg'=gf'$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with the same datum at all four corners, let $\theta=\theta_\square^{-1}=c_{f',g}\circ c_{g',f}^{-1}:L(g')^*Lf^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L(f')^*Lg^*$ be the inverse of the canonical ringed-square comparison $\theta_\square:L(f')^*Lg^*\to L(g')^*Lf^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Then
$$q_{g',n}\circ L(g')^*q_{f,n}=q_{f',n}\circ L(f')^*q_{g,n}\circ\theta_{Q_{Y,n}[0]}.$$
No properness or invertibility of an exchange map is assumed.

proof.text: Write $\rho_{u,n}:Q_{\mathrm{target}(u),n}\to u_*Q_{\mathrm{source}(u),n}$ for the adjunct of $a_{u,n}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] its underlying map is the canonical constant-section map. The projection identity $\pi_{U,n}c_u=c_{u,n}u^{-1}\pi_{V,n}$ makes this map coefficient-linear for the actions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Explicitly, in the tensor presentation the comparison is $x\otimes r\mapsto c_{u,n}(x)\pi_{U,n}(r)$. Transporting scalars along $c_u$ identifies this with the ring-sheaf isomorphism $c_{u,n}$ on the underlying module, so it is an isomorphism. Thus the stipulated normalization uses the actual module adjunction, rather than an independently chosen isomorphism of underlying sheaves.

source.place: Tag 03D3, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules; coefficient projection identities of lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image

proof.text:
The maps $\rho$ satisfy
$$\rho_{kh,n}=D_{h,k,Q_{Z,n}}\circ k_*\rho_{h,n}\circ\rho_{k,n}.$$
Indeed [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] presents $Q_{V,n}$ as the sheafification of the constant presheaf $P_n$. Precompose both proposed sheaf maps with its sheafification unit. On an object $U\to V$ and $p\in P_n$, the right side sends $p$ to $p$ over $W\times_VU$, then to $p$ over $Z\times_W(W\times_VU)$, and then restricts it to $Z\times_VU$. The left side sends it directly to that same constant section. The two presheaf maps therefore agree. The uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] proves equality of the sheaf maps, hence of the module maps. This argument does not suppose that all sections of a constant sheaf are globally constant.

Let $\eta_c$ be the unit of $(kh)^*\dashv(kh)_*$ and $\eta_{hk}$ the unit of $h^*k^*\dashv k_*h_*$. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] the latter hom bijection is the successive pair of hom bijections. The defining unit equation of the inverse conjugate $b$ in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] is
$$(kh)_*(b_M)\eta_{c,M}=D_{h,k,h^*k^*M}\eta_{hk,M}.$$
For $t:h^*k^*M\to N$, postcompose by $(kh)_*t$ and use naturality of $D$. It follows that the single-adjunction transpose of $t b_M$ equals $D_{h,k,N}$ followed after the composite-adjunction transpose of $t$. For $M=Q_{V,n}$, $N=Q_{Z,n}$ and $t=a_{h,n}\circ h^*a_{k,n}$, naturality of the two hom bijections makes that transpose $k_*\rho_{h,n}\circ\rho_{k,n}$. Step 2 identifies its composite with $D$ as $\rho_{kh,n}$. Injectivity of the single-adjunction hom bijection proves the asserted ordinary equality.

source.place: Tag 03D8, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; the adjunction-unit calculation is written out here

proof.text:
We check which ordinary comparison is being localized. Under the canonical inverse-image composition identification, the module comparison $b$ is
$$m\otimes r\longmapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes r.$$
Its inverse sends $(m\otimes s)\otimes r$ to $m\otimes c_h(h^{-1}s)r$. The tensor balancing relation gives both inverse identities; balancing over the remaining ring uses that the coefficient map for $kh$ is the composite of those for $k$ and $h$. These are sheaf maps because their formulas commute with restrictions. The units of the module adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] send $m$ to $m\otimes1$ after the underlying inverse-image unit. Hence these formulas satisfy the unit equation in step 3. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] identifies this tensor comparison with the specified $b$. In particular it is the termwise canonical module comparison used in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

source.place: Tag 03D8, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules; explicit tensor and unit calculation

proof.text: All three pullbacks are exact and their derived functors are induced termwise by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) to the termwise natural isomorphism $b$, followed by localization of complexes. This gives a derived comparison $\widehat b:L(kh)^*\to Lh^*Lk^*$ respecting the canonical factorization maps. It equals the specified $c_{h,k}$: for every complex $K$ choose $P\to K$ as in [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], on the site $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with ring sheaf $R_V$. At $P$ both comparisons are the class of the same termwise map by step 4 and the K-flat normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Naturality at the isomorphism represented by $P\to K$ then gives equality at $K$. Every derived object has such a representative. The coefficient transport is included here: the composite completed comparison equals $c_{kh}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], so the endpoint identification is exactly the one in the question.

For a module $M$ let $j(M)=M[0]$, and denote the exact-pullback comparison by $s_{u,M}:Lu^*j(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}j(u^*M)$. Termwise application gives $u^*(M[0])=(u^*M)[0]$ and the same identity for module maps. Thus $q_{u,n}=j(a_{u,n})s_{u,Q_{\mathrm{target}(u),n}}$. The descent formula of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2), with the identification of step 5, gives
$$s_{h,k^*M}\circ Lh^*(s_{k,M})\circ c_{h,k,j(M)}=j(b_M)\circ s_{kh,M}.$$
Naturality of $s_h$ with respect to $a_{k,n}$ now rewrites $q_{h,n}\circ Lh^*q_{k,n}\circ c_{h,k,j(Q_{V,n})}$ as $j(a_{h,n}\circ h^*a_{k,n}\circ b_{Q_{V,n}})s_{kh,Q_{V,n}}$. Step 3 makes this $j(a_{kh,n})s_{kh,Q_{V,n}}=q_{kh,n}$. Only functoriality and the canonical factorization maps of the exact operations were used.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, specialized through exact localization to single complexes

proof.text: For a quotient transition $t:P_b\to P_a$, the two composites of the normalized adjunct and $t$ send a constant $p$ to $t(p)$ on the base-changed object. The sheafification uniqueness used in step 2 makes them equal on the whole constant sheaf. By the projection and transition identities in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] these are maps of the required modules; transposing yields $a_{u,a}\circ u^*t=t\circ a_{u,b}$. For a morphism of finite ring systems $\phi_\bullet$, use the induced completed ring map and restrict target scalars along it. The equality $\phi_n\pi_n=\pi'_n\phi_\infty$ makes these maps linear after that restriction, and the same constant-section test sends $p$ to $\phi_n(p)$ on both sides. Exact restriction does not change underlying complexes. Functoriality of localization, including its respect for compositions, then gives the same naturality for the $q$'s. The composite equalities of steps 3 and 6 respect these maps because each factor does.

source.place: Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint; finite-system naturality of the coefficient comparison

proof.text:
In the chosen square, composition coherence of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] identifies the two completed coefficient maps along $fg'=gf'$. Put $A=q_{g',n}\circ L(g')^*q_{f,n}$ and $B=q_{f',n}\circ L(f')^*q_{g,n}$. Step 6 gives, after this specified equality transport,
$$A\circ c_{g',f}=q_{fg',n}=q_{gf',n}=B\circ c_{f',g}.$$
Here the two middle maps are identified by substituting the equality of the composite morphisms and coefficient maps; no arbitrary isomorphism is chosen. Right-compose with $c_{g',f}^{-1}$. This gives $A=B\circ c_{f',g}\circ c_{g',f}^{-1}$, the desired identity since [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] defines the inverse square comparison by precisely this product. Cancellation used only the pullback compositors, which are isomorphisms; it used no assertion about invertibility of exchange or properness.
